paragraphs.title: David Wants to Build a House for God, but God Defers the Building

answers: In his house of cedars
In the tabernacle
In Nathan’s house
easy.explanation: David said, “I dwell in an house of cedars,” while the ark remained under curtains.
easy.q: Where was David sitting when he thought about building a house for the LORD?

answers: Solomon
Nathan the prophet
The judges of Israel
easy.explanation: David told Nathan the prophet about his intention.
easy.q: To whom did David speak about his desire to build a house for the LORD?

answers: David would build the house immediately
Nathan would build the house
David would not build the house
easy.explanation: The LORD said, “Thou shalt not build me an house to dwell in.”
easy.q: What did the LORD tell David?

answers: He saw a contrast between his own house and the place of the ark
Nathan commanded him to build it
His enemies required him to build it
medium.explanation: David lived in a house of cedars, while the ark remained under curtains.
medium.q: Why did David want to build a house for the LORD?

answers: He immediately opposed it
He told David to do all that was in his heart
He asked David to delay the decision
medium.explanation: Nathan said, “Do all that is in thine heart; for God is with thee.”
medium.q: How did Nathan initially respond to David’s desire?

answers: Royal garments
Musical instruments
Cloth coverings or tent material
medium.explanation: Here, “curtains” refers to the fabric coverings of a tent or tabernacle.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does “curtains” mean in the phrase “the ark of the covenant of the LORD remaineth under curtains”?

answers: The strength of David versus the weakness of Nathan
David’s house of cedars versus the tent where the ark remained
Israel versus the nations around it
challenge.explanation: David lived in a cedar house, while the ark was under curtains.
challenge.q: What main contrast led David to think about building the house?

answers: The desire was good, but David was not chosen to carry it out
The desire was sinful, so David was punished
The desire was unknown to God
challenge.explanation: The LORD prevented David from building the house but did not describe his desire as sinful.
challenge.q: What do the LORD’s words show about David’s desire?

answers: To explain that He had never required this from Israel’s previous leaders
To show that the ark was unimportant
To abolish the rule of the judges
challenge.explanation: The LORD said He had not commanded any of Israel’s judges to build Him such a house.
challenge.q: Why did the LORD say that He had not asked Israel’s former leaders to build Him a house of cedars?

paragraphs.title: God’s Promise to David and His House

answers: From the sheepcote and from following the sheep
From the priests’ house
From Jerusalem
easy.explanation: The LORD reminded David that He took him from the sheep and made him ruler over Israel.
easy.q: From where did the LORD take David?

answers: He hid them
He subdued or cut them off
He made them kings
easy.explanation: The LORD said He had cut off David’s enemies and would subdue them.
easy.q: What did the LORD do to David’s enemies?

answers: David himself
One of Israel’s judges
David’s seed after him
easy.explanation: The LORD promised to raise up David’s seed, who would build Him a house.
easy.q: Who would build a house for the LORD according to the promise?

answers: He took him from the sheep, made him ruler, and protected him
He made him a prophet
He returned him to shepherding
medium.explanation: The LORD described choosing David, making him ruler, and being with him wherever he went.
medium.q: What had the LORD done for David before promising him a royal house?

answers: David would build a house, and then his seed would reign
The LORD would build David a royal house, and David’s seed would build the house for God
David would leave the kingdom, and Nathan would replace him
medium.explanation: Instead of David building a house for God, the LORD promised to establish David’s royal house.
medium.q: What is the main order of events in the LORD’s promise?

answers: Only a residence
A military camp
A royal family and dynasty
medium.explanation: In this context, “house” means an enduring royal dynasty.
medium.q: What does “house” mean in “the LORD will build thee an house”?

answers: David wants to build a house for God, but God promises to build a house for David
David asks for a kingdom, but God offers him shepherding
David asks for peace, but God promises war
challenge.explanation: The LORD reverses the direction of the request: He will establish David’s house.
challenge.q: What is the central reversal between David’s request and the LORD’s answer?

answers: It will last only during David’s lifetime
The kingdom and throne will be established for ever
It will be replaced immediately after David dies
challenge.explanation: The LORD repeatedly promises an everlasting kingdom and throne.
challenge.q: What is promised concerning David’s house?

answers: The LORD will be his Father, and he will be God’s son
The LORD will be his servant, and he will be God’s king
The LORD will be his enemy, and he will be God’s judge
challenge.explanation: The LORD says, “I will be his father, and he shall be my son.”
challenge.q: What relationship does the LORD describe between Himself and David’s descendant?

paragraphs.title: David’s Response to the Prophecy and the Dynastic Promise

answers: Before the LORD
At the city gate
In the house of cedars
easy.explanation: David came and sat before the LORD.
easy.q: Where did David sit after hearing Nathan’s words?

answers: As greater than all kings
As unworthy of such great kindness
As leaders chosen only by the people
easy.explanation: David humbly asked, “Who am I, O LORD God, and what is mine house?”
easy.q: How did David describe himself and his house?

answers: As one nation in the earth
As many separate peoples
As a people without a ruler
easy.explanation: David asked, “What one nation in the earth is like thy people Israel?”

answers: That the LORD had chosen him and his house and brought him to this position
That Nathan had built the house
That his enemies had become kings
medium.explanation: David marveled at the kindness shown to him and the position to which God had brought him.
medium.q: What did David acknowledge at the beginning of his prayer?

answers: His riches only
His uniqueness and the fact that there is no God beside Him
The strength of Israel’s army alone
medium.explanation: David said, “There is none like thee, neither is there any God beside thee.”
medium.q: What did David praise about the LORD?

answers: The LORD redeemed Israel and chose it to be His people
Israel chose the LORD only after the kingdom was established
The LORD separated Israel from all other nations
medium.explanation: David recalled that God redeemed Israel to be His own people.
medium.q: What relationship between the LORD and Israel did David describe?

answers: Pride in his power
Humility and wonder at God’s kindness
Anger that the house would not be built
challenge.explanation: David emphasizes his smallness and the greatness of the kindness shown to him.
challenge.q: What does David’s question, “Who am I... and what is mine house?” reveal about his response?

answers: To praise God’s deliverance and choice of Israel
To describe the construction of David’s palace
To explain why Nathan opposed him
challenge.explanation: David praised God for redeeming Israel and making His name great.
challenge.q: Why did David mention God redeeming Israel from Egypt?

answers: Both were chosen and made special through God’s kindness
Both wanted to build a house of cedars
Both had formerly been enemies of Israel
challenge.explanation: David marvels at his own calling while also praising God’s choice of Israel.
challenge.q: What idea is shared by David’s description of himself and his description of Israel?

paragraphs.title: David Prays for the Fulfillment of the Promise

answers: That they would be erased
That they would be established for ever
That they would remain secret
easy.explanation: David asked that the LORD’s words be established for ever.
easy.q: What did David ask concerning the words spoken about God’s servant and his house?

answers: That it would be established before the LORD
That it would disappear after one generation
That it would be given to Nathan
easy.explanation: David asked that the house of his servant be established before the LORD.
easy.q: What did David ask concerning the house of David?

answers: His intention to build David a house
The names of all David’s enemies
Nathan’s place of residence
easy.explanation: David said that God had told him He would build him a house.
easy.q: What had the LORD made known to David, according to David’s prayer?

answers: The LORD had revealed His promise and blessed David’s house
David had already built the Temple
Nathan had promised him victory in war
medium.explanation: David prayed because God had revealed His promise and promised goodness to him.
medium.q: Why did David find encouragement to pray before the LORD?

answers: The name of the LORD
The house of cedars alone
The power of Israel’s enemies
medium.explanation: David asked that the LORD’s name be magnified for ever.
medium.q: What did David ask to be magnified for ever?

answers: You have refused this goodness
You have promised or pledged this goodness
You have forgotten this goodness
medium.explanation: The phrase means that God had promised or pledged this goodness to David.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does “hast promised” mean in “thou art God, and hast promised this goodness unto thy servant”?

answers: David asks that the blessing already given to his house remain firm and enduring
David asks that the blessing be canceled
David asks that the blessing be given only to his enemies
challenge.explanation: David asks that the words concerning his servant and his house be established for ever.
challenge.q: What is the connection between David’s request for the promise to be established and God’s blessing of his house?

answers: As a good promise and blessing for which he should give thanks
As a threat that must be rejected
As something unrelated to him
challenge.explanation: David recognizes the promise as goodness and asks the LORD to bless his house.
challenge.q: How does David regard the LORD’s promise at the end of his prayer?

answers: David’s house and kingdom will remain established before the LORD
David will immediately give up the kingdom
Israel will remain without a royal house
challenge.explanation: David asks that his house be established before God for ever.
challenge.q: What future is implied by the promise discussed in this passage?
